content: Pyridoxine deficiency, also known as vitamin B6 deficiency, is characterized by a range of clinical manifestations. These include a seborrheic dermatitis-like skin eruption, atrophic glossitis with ulceration, angular cheilitis, conjunctivitis, intertrigo, and neurological symptoms such as somnolence, confusion, and peripheral neuropathy. Vitamin B6 serves as a critical co-factor for the enzyme glutamic acid decarboxylase, which is responsible for converting glutamate into gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA), an inhibitory neurotransmitter. In the context of vitamin B6 deficiency, there is an imbalance in neurotransmitter levels, with an increase in the excitatory neurotransmitter glutamate and a decrease in GABA. This imbalance can lead to the development of seizures as a clinical manifestation of the deficiency.
